claim: The vacuole membrane requires the two-pore channel TPC1 (formerly called SV channel) to fire action-potential-like electrical signals.
source: To fire action-potential-like electrical signals, the vacuole membrane requires the two-pore channel TPC1, formerly called SV channel.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a direct assertion about TPC1's role in vacuole electrical signaling.

claim: The TPC1/SV channel functions as a depolarization-stimulated, non-selective cation channel.
source: The TPC1/SV channel functions as a depolarization-stimulated, non-selective cation channel that is inhibited by luminal Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a characterization of TPC1 channel properties.

claim: The TPC1/SV channel is inhibited by luminal Ca2+.
source: The TPC1/SV channel functions as a depolarization-stimulated, non-selective cation channel that is inhibited by luminal Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a property of TPC1 channels.

claim: Three acidic residues are present in Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 of the Ca2+-sensitive AtTPC1 channel from Arabidopsis thaliana.
source: In our search for species-dependent functional TPC1 channel variants with different luminal Ca2+ sensitivity, we found in total three acidic residues present in Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 of the Ca2+-sensitive AtTPC1 channel from Arabidopsis thaliana that were neutral in its Vicia faba ortholog and also in those of many other Fabaceae.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on sequence analysis and comparison.

claim: Three acidic residues in Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 of AtTPC1 are neutral in the Vicia faba ortholog.
source: In our search for species-dependent functional TPC1 channel variants with different luminal Ca2+ sensitivity, we found in total three acidic residues present in Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 of the Ca2+-sensitive AtTPC1 channel from Arabidopsis thaliana that were neutral in its Vicia faba ortholog and also in those of many other Fabaceae.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on sequence comparison.

claim: Three acidic residues in Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 of AtTPC1 are neutral in many other Fabaceae TPC1 orthologs.
source: In our search for species-dependent functional TPC1 channel variants with different luminal Ca2+ sensitivity, we found in total three acidic residues present in Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 of the Ca2+-sensitive AtTPC1 channel from Arabidopsis thaliana that were neutral in its Vicia faba ortholog and also in those of many other Fabaceae.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on sequence analysis across Fabaceae species.

claim: Wild-type VfTPC1 is hypersensitive to vacuole depolarization when expressed in the Arabidopsis AtTPC1-loss-of-function background.
source: When expressed in the Arabidopsis AtTPC1-loss-of-function background, wild-type VfTPC1 was hypersensitive to vacuole depolarization and only weakly sensitive to blocking luminal Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on experimental observations.

claim: Wild-type VfTPC1 is only weakly sensitive to blocking luminal Ca2+ when expressed in the Arabidopsis AtTPC1-loss-of-function background.
source: When expressed in the Arabidopsis AtTPC1-loss-of-function background, wild-type VfTPC1 was hypersensitive to vacuole depolarization and only weakly sensitive to blocking luminal Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on experimental observations.

claim: Two neutral substitutions in Ca2+ sensor site 3 are sufficient for the Arabidopsis At-VfTPC1 channel mutant to gain VfTPC1-like voltage sensitivity.
source: When AtTPC1 was mutated for these VfTPC1-homologous polymorphic residues, two neutral substitutions in Ca2+ sensor site 3 alone were already sufficient for the Arabidopsis At-VfTPC1 channel mutant to gain VfTPC1-like voltage and luminal Ca2+ sensitivity that together rendered vacuoles hyperexcitable.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on mutagenesis experiments.

claim: Two neutral substitutions in Ca2+ sensor site 3 are sufficient for the Arabidopsis At-VfTPC1 channel mutant to gain VfTPC1-like luminal Ca2+ sensitivity.
source: When AtTPC1 was mutated for these VfTPC1-homologous polymorphic residues, two neutral substitutions in Ca2+ sensor site 3 alone were already sufficient for the Arabidopsis At-VfTPC1 channel mutant to gain VfTPC1-like voltage and luminal Ca2+ sensitivity that together rendered vacuoles hyperexcitable.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on mutagenesis experiments.

claim: VfTPC1-like voltage and luminal Ca2+ sensitivity together render vacuoles hyperexcitable.
source: When AtTPC1 was mutated for these VfTPC1-homologous polymorphic residues, two neutral substitutions in Ca2+ sensor site 3 alone were already sufficient for the Arabidopsis At-VfTPC1 channel mutant to gain VfTPC1-like voltage and luminal Ca2+ sensitivity that together rendered vacuoles hyperexcitable.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on experimental observations.

claim: Natural TPC1 channel variants exist in plant families which may fine-tune vacuole excitability.
source: Thus, natural TPC1 channel variants exist in plant families which may fine-tune vacuole excitability and adapt it to environmental settings of the particular ecological niche.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion based on the findings.

claim: Natural TPC1 channel variants may adapt vacuole excitability to environmental settings of the particular ecological niche.
source: Thus, natural TPC1 channel variants exist in plant families which may fine-tune vacuole excitability and adapt it to environmental settings of the particular ecological niche.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a speculative conclusion.

claim: The SV channel was identified as a calcium-regulated, voltage-dependent cation channel soon after the patch-clamp technique was first applied to plant cells.
source: Soon after the patch-clamp technique was first applied to plant cells (for review see Hedrich and Marten, 2011; Schroeder and Hedrich, 1989), the slow vacuolar (SV) channel was identified as a calcium-regulated, voltage-dependent cation channel (Allen and Sanders, 1996; Amodeo et al., 1994; Bethke and Jones, 1994; Colombo et al., 1988; Hedrich and Neher, 1987; Pottosin et al., 2001; Ward and Schroeder, 1994, for review see Pottosin and Dobrovinskaya, 2022; Ward, 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations supporting the historical context.

claim: The SV channel is similarly permeable for Na+ and K+.
source: The SV channel is similarly permeable for Na+ and K+, and in principle also to Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a known property of the SV channel.

claim: The SV channel is in principle permeable to Ca2+.
source: The SV channel is similarly permeable for Na+ and K+, and in principle also to Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a known property of the SV channel.

claim: The physiological relevance of a potential Ca2+ permeability of the SV channel in planta is highly controversial.
source: However, the physiological relevance of a potential Ca2+ permeability in planta is highly controversial (for review see Hedrich et al., 2018; Pottosin and Dobrovinskaya, 2022), a view further supported – among other studies – by recent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations (Navarro-Retamal et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to reviews and MD simulations.

claim: Peiter et al., 2005 revealed that the Arabidopsis thaliana SV channel is encoded by the single copy gene TPC1.
source: About two decades after the discovery of SV channels, Peiter et al., 2005 revealed that the Arabidopsis thaliana SV channel is encoded by the single copy gene TPC1.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to the original discovery.

claim: TPC1 is not responsible for global Ca2+ responses but contributes to long-distance electrical and Ca2+ signaling under salt stress conditions.
source: Studies on AtTPC1 mutant plants suggest that TPC1 is not responsible for global Ca2+ responses but contributes to long-distance electrical and Ca2+ signaling under salt stress conditions and is an essential player in vacuole excitability (Bellandi et al., 2022; Choi et al., 2014; Evans et al., 2016; Jaślan et al., 2019; Ranf et al., 2008, for review see Hedrich et al., 2018; Pottosin and Dobrovinskaya, 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations to studies on AtTPC1 mutants.

claim: TPC1 is an essential player in vacuole excitability.
source: Studies on AtTPC1 mutant plants suggest that TPC1 is not responsible for global Ca2+ responses but contributes to long-distance electrical and Ca2+ signaling under salt stress conditions and is an essential player in vacuole excitability (Bellandi et al., 2022; Choi et al., 2014; Evans et al., 2016; Jaślan et al., 2019; Ranf et al., 2008, for review see Hedrich et al., 2018; Pottosin and Dobrovinskaya, 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations to studies on AtTPC1 mutants.

claim: Characteristic structural fingerprints of TPC1-type channels remained unchanged from mosses to flowering plants during land plant evolution.
source: During land plant evolution characteristic structural fingerprints of TPC1-type channels remained unchanged from mosses to flowering plants (Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2011; Dreyer et al., 2021; Hedrich et al., 1988).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to evolutionary studies.

claim: Both the crystal and cryoEM structure of the Arabidopsis AtTPC1 channel became available recently.
source: Recently, both the crystal and cryoEM structure of the Arabidopsis AtTPC1 channel and thus the molecular topology of this vacuolar cation channel became available (Dickinson et al., 2022; Guo et al., 2016; Kintzer and Stroud, 2016; Ye et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to structural studies.

claim: AtTPC1 is formed by a dimer whose monomers consist of two tandem Shaker-like cassettes, each with six transmembrane domains (TM1–6), connected by a cytoplasmic loop with two EF hands.
source: AtTPC1 is formed by a dimer whose monomers consist of two tandem Shaker-like cassettes, each with six transmembrane domains (TM1–6), connected by a cytoplasmic loop with two EF hands.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a structural description of AtTPC1.

claim: Calcium binding to the EF hands is necessary for SV/TPC1 channel activation at elevated cytosolic Ca2+ levels.
source: Calcium binding to the EF hands is necessary for SV/TPC1 channel activation at elevated cytosolic Ca2+ levels (Guo et al., 2016; Schulze et al., 2011; Ye et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to functional studies.

claim: The major voltage-sensing domain (VSD) required for depolarization-dependent activation in each monomer is in the first four transmembrane segments of the second Shaker-like cassette.
source: Structural 3D motif comparison and point mutation analysis identified the major voltage-sensing domain (VSD) required for depolarization-dependent activation in each monomer in the first four transmembrane segments of the second Shaker-like cassette (Guo et al., 2016; Jaślan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to structural and mutagenesis studies.

claim: Activation of VSD2 is required for Ca2+ activation of the EF hand domain.
source: CryoEM structures further suggested that activation of VSD2 is required for Ca2+ activation of the EF hand domain (Ye et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a cryoEM study.

claim: Channel activation is strongly suppressed when the Ca2+ level in the vacuolar lumen reaches 1 mM and more.
source: In contrast, channel activation is strongly suppressed when the Ca2+ level in the vacuolar lumen reaches 1 mM and more (Guo et al., 2016; Jaślan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to functional studies.

claim: Luminal Ca2+ can bind to three non-canonical calcium-binding sites each formed by three acidic residues in AtTPC1.
source: Luminal Ca2+ can bind to three non-canonical calcium-binding sites each formed by three acidic residues in AtTPC1 (site 1: D240, D454, and E528; site 2: E239, D240, and E457; site 3: E605, D606, and D607; Dickinson et al., 2022; Guo et al., 2016; Kintzer and Stroud, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to structural studies.

claim: Site 1 residues are located in luminal linker regions between transmembrane domains.
source: Site 1/2 residues are located in luminal linker regions between transmembrane domains while site 3 residues are found in the luminal pore entrance.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a structural description.

claim: Site 2 residues are located in luminal linker regions between transmembrane domains.
source: Site 1/2 residues are located in luminal linker regions between transmembrane domains while site 3 residues are found in the luminal pore entrance.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a structural description.

claim: Site 3 residues are found in the luminal pore entrance.
source: Site 1/2 residues are located in luminal linker regions between transmembrane domains while site 3 residues are found in the luminal pore entrance.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a structural description.

claim: Sites 1 and 3 play key roles in voltage gating and luminal Ca2+ inhibition.
source: Among them, sites 1 and 3 play key roles in voltage gating and luminal Ca2+ inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a functional characterization.

claim: The TPC1 mutant fou2 was identified by screening a chemically induced Arabidopsis mutant collection for individuals producing elevated amounts of the wound hormone jasmonate (JA).
source: Screening a chemically induced Arabidopsis mutant collection for individuals producing elevated amounts of the wound hormone jasmonate (JA) identified the TPC1 mutant fou2 (fatty acid oxygenation upregulated 2) (Bonaventure et al., 2007a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to the original discovery.

claim: The fou2 channel behaves like a hyperactive TPC1 channel.
source: Interestingly, the fou2 channel behaves like a hyperactive TPC1 channel (Beyhl et al., 2009; Bonaventure et al., 2007a) and opens already close to the vacuole resting voltage which is around –30 mV (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to functional studies.

claim: The fou2 channel opens already close to the vacuole resting voltage which is around –30 mV.
source: Interestingly, the fou2 channel behaves like a hyperactive TPC1 channel (Beyhl et al., 2009; Bonaventure et al., 2007a) and opens already close to the vacuole resting voltage which is around –30 mV (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to functional studies.

claim: Wild-type AtTPC1 becomes active only upon depolarization.
source: In contrast, wild-type AtTPC1 becomes active only upon depolarization.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a contrast to fou2.

claim: The hypersensitivity of the fou2 TPC1 channel toward voltage confers hyperexcitability to the vacuole.
source: The hypersensitivity of the fou2 TPC1 channel toward voltage confers hyperexcitability to the vacuole and results from a mutation of the negatively charged glutamate at position 454 to the uncharged asparagine (D454N) (Bonaventure et al., 2007a; Jaślan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to functional studies.

claim: The hypersensitivity of the fou2 TPC1 channel toward voltage results from a mutation of the negatively charged glutamate at position 454 to the uncharged asparagine (D454N).
source: The hypersensitivity of the fou2 TPC1 channel toward voltage confers hyperexcitability to the vacuole and results from a mutation of the negatively charged glutamate at position 454 to the uncharged asparagine (D454N) (Bonaventure et al., 2007a; Jaślan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to functional studies.

claim: The TPC1 site at position 454 is directed toward the vacuole lumen and is part of the non-canonical Ca2+ sensor site 1.
source: This TPC1 site is directed toward the vacuole lumen and is part of the non-canonical Ca2+ sensor site 1 (Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2011; Guo et al., 2016; Kintzer and Stroud, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to structural studies.

claim: The block of channel activity by elevated luminal Ca2+ levels, typical for wild-type TPC1, is greatly attenuated in the fou2 mutant.
source: Therefore, the block of channel activity by elevated luminal Ca2+ levels, typical for wild-type TPC1, is greatly attenuated in the fou2 mutant (Lenglet et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a functional study.

claim: fou2 vacuoles must experience episodes in which the membrane potential is short circuited.
source: Consequently, fou2 vacuoles must experience episodes in which the membrane potential is short circuited.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from the fou2 phenotype.

claim: fou2 plants appear wounded and produce large amounts of jasmonate.
source: As a result, fou2 plants appear wounded and produce large amounts of jasmonate (Bonaventure et al., 2007a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to the original study.

claim: Strong membrane depolarizations triggered by current injection into healthy Arabidopsis leaves strongly activated the JA pathway.
source: Interestingly, strong membrane depolarizations triggered by current injection into healthy Arabidopsis leaves strongly activated the JA pathway, suggesting a link between vacuolar membrane potential and activation of JA synthesis (Mousavi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to an experimental study.

claim: Additional luminal amino acids other than the central Ca2+-binding sites like D454 are involved in luminal Ca2+ sensing, for example the adjacent E457 from Ca2+ sensor site 2.
source: Functional studies in the context of the fou2 mutation site showed that additional luminal amino acids other than the central Ca2+-binding sites like D454 are involved in luminal Ca2+ sensing, for example the adjacent E457 from Ca2+ sensor site 2 (Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2011; Guo et al., 2016; Kintzer and Stroud, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to functional and structural studies.

claim: Neutralization of E457 desensitized AtTPC1 toward vacuolar Ca2+ but unlike the fou2 mutation did not additionally promote channel opening.
source: Neutralization of E457 desensitized AtTPC1 toward vacuolar Ca2+ but unlike the fou2 mutation did not additionally promote channel opening (Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a functional study.

claim: The TPC1 channels from Vicia faba and A. thaliana are historically established prototypes of the SV channel.
source: The TPC1 channels from Vicia faba and A. thaliana are historically established prototypes of the SV channel.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as historical context.

claim: Only AtTPC1 but not VfTPC1 has been identified at the molecular level so far.
source: Nevertheless, only AtTPC1 but not VfTPC1 has been identified at the molecular level so far.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in knowledge.

claim: SV currents had been recorded from V. faba guard cell vacuoles even under unnatural high luminal Ca2+ loads (50 mM).
source: In our search for natural TPC1 channel variants, we noticed that SV currents had been recorded from V. faba guard cell vacuoles even under unnatural high luminal Ca2+ loads (50 mM; Ward and Schroeder, 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to the original observation.

claim: Hardly any AtTPC1/SV currents were recorded in A. thaliana mesophyll vacuoles even at a lower luminal Ca2+ level such as 10 mM.
source: Considering that hardly any AtTPC1/SV currents were recorded in A. thaliana mesophyll vacuoles even at a lower luminal Ca2+ level such as 10 mM (Lenglet et al., 2017), the TPC1 channel variants of V. faba and A. thaliana seem to differ in their Ca2+ sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to a functional study.

claim: The TPC1 channel variants of V. faba and A. thaliana seem to differ in their Ca2+ sensitivity.
source: Considering that hardly any AtTPC1/SV currents were recorded in A. thaliana mesophyll vacuoles even at a lower luminal Ca2+ level such as 10 mM (Lenglet et al., 2017), the TPC1 channel variants of V. faba and A. thaliana seem to differ in their Ca2+ sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from previous observations.

claim: A single VfTPC1 transcript was identified following RNA-seq and de novo transcriptome assembly from fava bean.
source: To gain insights into the molecular structure and function of VfTPC1, we isolated RNA from fava bean. Following RNA-seq and de novo transcriptome assembly, we identified a single VfTPC1 transcript, just as in A. thaliana (Peiter et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq data.

claim: VfTPC1 was found to localize exclusively to the vacuole membrane as visualized by the fluorescent eYFP signal.
source: Similar to TPC1 from Arabidopsis (Figure 1) and other plant species (Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2013), VfTPC1 was found to localize exclusively to the vacuole membrane as visualized by the fluorescent eYFP signal (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1 showing fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Macroscopic outward-rectifying SV/TPC1-like currents were elicited upon depolarizing voltage pulses in whole-vacuole patch-clamp experiments with fluorescent mesophyll vacuoles expressing VfTPC1.
source: In whole-vacuole patch-clamp experiments with such fluorescent mesophyll vacuoles, macroscopic outward-rectifying SV/TPC1-like currents were elicited upon depolarizing voltage pulses (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2 showing patch-clamp recordings.

claim: VfTPC1 channels differed from AtTPC1 in kinetics, voltage dependence, and luminal calcium sensitivity.
source: However, compared to AtTPC1, VfTPC1 channels differed in kinetics, voltage dependence, and luminal calcium sensitivity (Figures 2—5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 2-5 showing electrophysiological data.

claim: The current activation was faster with VfTPC1 than with AtTPC1 in the presence of physiological-like luminal Mg2+ (2 mM) but absence of luminal Ca2+.
source: In the presence of physiological-like luminal Mg2+ (2 mM) (Shaul, 2002) but absence of luminal Ca2+, the current activation was faster and the current deactivation slower with VfTPC1 than with AtTPC1 (Figures 2A—4A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 2-4 showing kinetic data.

claim: The current deactivation was slower with VfTPC1 than with AtTPC1 in the presence of physiological-like luminal Mg2+ (2 mM) but absence of luminal Ca2+.
source: In the presence of physiological-like luminal Mg2+ (2 mM) (Shaul, 2002) but absence of luminal Ca2+, the current activation was faster and the current deactivation slower with VfTPC1 than with AtTPC1 (Figures 2A—4A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 2-4 showing kinetic data.

claim: Inward currents were triggered by voltages in the range of −40 and 0 mV from vacuoles harboring VfTPC1 and not AtTPC1.
source: A closer look at the current–voltage curves further revealed that in addition to outward currents, inward currents were also triggered by voltages in the range of −40 and 0 mV, but only from vacuoles harboring VfTPC1 and not AtTPC1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1 showing current-voltage curves.

claim: The voltage activation threshold for VfTPC1 channel opening is shifted by about 30 mV to more negative voltages compared to AtTPC1.
source: This points to a shift in the voltage activation threshold for VfTPC1 channel opening by about 30 mV to more negative voltages.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the current-voltage data.

claim: The midpoint voltage V1 of VfTPC1 is −3.5 ± 12.3 mV (n = 5).
source: From these fits the midpoint voltages V2 and V1 were derived (Figure 5B), showing in particular, a significant difference in midpoint voltage V1 of VfTPC1 (−3.5 ± 12.3 mV, n = 5) and AtTPC1 (51.2 ± 9.6 mV, n = 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis of voltage-dependent open-channel probability curves shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The midpoint voltage V1 of AtTPC1 is 51.2 ± 9.6 mV (n = 5).
source: From these fits the midpoint voltages V2 and V1 were derived (Figure 5B), showing in particular, a significant difference in midpoint voltage V1 of VfTPC1 (−3.5 ± 12.3 mV, n = 5) and AtTPC1 (51.2 ± 9.6 mV, n = 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis of voltage-dependent open-channel probability curves shown in Figure 5B.

claim: VfTPC1, unlike AtTPC1, activates near the vacuolar resting membrane voltage.
source: These results confirm that VfTPC1, unlike AtTPC1, activates near the vacuolar resting membrane voltage (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the midpoint voltage data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: When the luminal Ca2+ concentration was increased from 0 to 10 mM Ca2+, the activation kinetics of AtTPC1 was strongly slowed down.
source: When the luminal Ca2+ concentration was increased from 0 to 10 mM Ca2+, the activation kinetics of AtTPC1 was strongly slowed down (Figure 3B, C, E, F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3 showing kinetic data.

claim: The effect of luminal Ca2+ on activation kinetics was much less pronounced for VfTPC1 than for AtTPC1.
source: However, this effect was much less pronounced for VfTPC1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a comparison of Ca2+ effects on the two channels.

claim: At +90 mV, the half-activation time increased by about 170% for AtTPC1 when luminal Ca2+ was increased from 0 to 10 mM.
source: At +90 mV, for example, the half-activation time increased by about 170% for AtTPC1, but only 53% for VfTPC1 (Figure 3A–C, E, F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3 showing kinetic data.

claim: At +90 mV, the half-activation time increased by only 53% for VfTPC1 when luminal Ca2+ was increased from 0 to 10 mM.
source: At +90 mV, for example, the half-activation time increased by about 170% for AtTPC1, but only 53% for VfTPC1 (Figure 3A–C, E, F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3 showing kinetic data.

claim: AtTPC1 currents were suppressed by about 50% at 10 mM luminal Ca2+.
source: Even more impressive was the fact that AtTPC1 currents were suppressed by about 50% at 10 mM luminal Ca2+ and completely vanished at 50 mM luminal Ca2+ (Figure 2), the concentration used in the very early work on SV currents from fava bean (Ward and Schroeder, 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2 showing current-voltage data.

claim: AtTPC1 currents completely vanished at 50 mM luminal Ca2+.
source: Even more impressive was the fact that AtTPC1 currents were suppressed by about 50% at 10 mM luminal Ca2+ and completely vanished at 50 mM luminal Ca2+ (Figure 2), the concentration used in the very early work on SV currents from fava bean (Ward and Schroeder, 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2 showing current-voltage data.

claim: The VfTPC1 current densities at zero and 10 mM luminal Ca2+ were similar in magnitude.
source: In contrast, the VfTPC1 current densities at zero and 10 mM luminal Ca2+ were similar in magnitude, and at 50 mM Ca2+ the VfTPC1 current density still reached about 50% of the level measured under luminal Ca2+-free conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a comparison of VfTPC1 behavior at different Ca2+ concentrations.

claim: At 50 mM Ca2+ the VfTPC1 current density still reached about 50% of the level measured under luminal Ca2+-free conditions.
source: In contrast, the VfTPC1 current densities at zero and 10 mM luminal Ca2+ were similar in magnitude, and at 50 mM Ca2+ the VfTPC1 current density still reached about 50% of the level measured under luminal Ca2+-free conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a comparison of VfTPC1 behavior at different Ca2+ concentrations.

claim: At 10 mM Ca2+, the V1 and V2 values increased by about 115 and 61 mV for AtTPC1 compared to 0 mM Ca2+.
source: Compared to 0 mM Ca2+, at 10 mM Ca2+ the V1 and V2 values increased by about 115 and 61 mV for AtTPC1, but only by about 61 and 26 mV for VfTPC1, respectively (Figure 5B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5 showing voltage activation data.

claim: At 10 mM Ca2+, the V1 and V2 values increased by only about 61 and 26 mV for VfTPC1 compared to 0 mM Ca2+.
source: Compared to 0 mM Ca2+, at 10 mM Ca2+ the V1 and V2 values increased by about 115 and 61 mV for AtTPC1, but only by about 61 and 26 mV for VfTPC1, respectively (Figure 5B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5 showing voltage activation data.

claim: A rise from 10 to 50 mM luminal Ca2+ caused a further positive-going shift of the VfTPC1 activation voltage curve (G/Gmax(V)), indicated by a 1.7- and 1.6-fold rise in V1 and V2, respectively.
source: A rise from 10 to 50 mM luminal Ca2+ caused a further positive-going shift of the VfTPC1 activation voltage curve (G/Gmax(V)), indicated by a 1.7- and 1.6-fold rise in V1 and V2, respectively (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5 showing voltage activation data.

claim: VfTPC1 is much less susceptible to inhibitory luminal Ca2+ than AtTPC1.
source: Together these findings document that VfTPC1 is much less susceptible to inhibitory luminal Ca2+ than AtTPC1.

claim: The three sites involved in luminal Ca2+ coordination and sensitivity in AtTPC1 were highly conserved among the Brassicaceae TPC1s.
source: Focusing on charged residues at the three sites that are involved in luminal Ca2+ coordination and sensitivity in AtTPC1 (Figure 5; Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2011; Dickinson et al., 2022; Kintzer and Stroud, 2016), we found that these sites were highly conserved among the Brassicaceae TPC1s.

evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on sequence alignment.

claim: Most TPC1 types of the Fabaceae species show one up to three non-conservative variations of the residues at the three Ca2+ sensor sites.
source: In contrast, most TPC1 types of the Fabaceae species show one up to three non-conservative variations of the residues.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on sequence alignment.

claim: Eleven of the 14 Fabaceae TPC1 channels harbor a non-charged asparagine or glutamine instead of the negatively charged glutamate at sites homologous to AtTPC1-E456 or -E457.
source: Eleven of the 14 Fabaceae TPC1 channels harbor a non-charged asparagine or glutamine instead of the negatively charged glutamate at sites homologous to AtTPC1-E456 or -E457 (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6 showing sequence alignment.

claim: The Fabaceae TPC1 channels group in two clusters, containing either one or two non-charged residues (Ala/Val, Asn) at the homologous sites to AtTPC1-E605 and -D606.

claim: The fava bean TPC1 channel belongs to a triple-polymorphism subgroup, containing alanine and asparagine at sites homologous to the Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 of AtTPC1.

claim: All TPC1 channel mutants (VfTPC1 triple mutant N458E/A607E/N608D and AtTPC1 double and triple mutants E605A/D606N and E457N/E605A/D606N) were localized in the vacuole membrane when transiently expressed in the background of the attpc1-2 mutant.

claim: All TPC1 channel mutants gave rise to the typical SV/TPC1 channel currents.
source: When transiently expressed in the background of the attpc1-2 mutant (Figure 1 and Figure 7A), all these channel mutants were localized in the vacuole membrane and gave rise to the typical SV/TPC1 channel currents (Figures 2A and 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 2A and 7B showing patch-clamp recordings.

claim: No significant differences were found between VfTPC1 wild type and its triple mutant with respect to their voltage dependence and luminal Ca2+ sensitivity.
source: When the two VfTPC1 channel variants were examined with respect to their voltage dependence and luminal Ca2+ sensitivity, no significant differences were found between VfTPC1 wild type and its triple mutant (Figure 7C–G).

claim: The double AtTPC1 mutant activated significantly faster than AtTPC1 wild type under luminal Ca2+-free conditions.

claim: The triple AtTPC1 mutant did not activate significantly faster than AtTPC1 wild type under luminal Ca2+-free conditions.
source: Compared to AtTPC1 wild type, the double but not the triple AtTPC1 mutant activated significantly faster under luminal Ca2+-free conditions (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3 showing kinetic data.

claim: The lack of effect on activation of the AtTPC1 triple mutant is likely related to the attenuating influence of the mutated residue E457N.
source: The lack of effect on activation of the AtTPC1 triple mutant is likely related to the attenuating influence of the mutated residue E457N, because Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2011 showed that the activation kinetics of the single AtTPC1 mutant E457N were slowed down.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference based on previous findings.

claim: The deactivation of both the double and triple AtTPC1 mutants was not much affected and was more AtTPC1- than VfTPC1-like.
source: The deactivation of both, the double and triple AtTPC1 mutants, however, was not much affected and was more AtTPC1- than VfTPC1-like (Figure 4), suggesting that other functional domains than Ca2+ sensor site 3 determines the deactivation behavior of TPC1 channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4 showing deactivation kinetics.

claim: Other functional domains than Ca2+ sensor site 3 determine the deactivation behavior of TPC1 channels.
source: The deactivation of both, the double and triple AtTPC1 mutants, however, was not much affected and was more AtTPC1- than VfTPC1-like (Figure 4), suggesting that other functional domains than Ca2+ sensor site 3 determines the deactivation behavior of TPC1 channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the deactivation data.

claim: Deactivation of the PpTPC1a channel from the moss Physcomitrella patens was slower than that of AtTPC1, although all three luminal Ca2+ sensor sites 1–3 were functional.
source: This view is also supported by the fact that deactivation of the PpTPC1a channel from the moss Physcomitrella patens was slower than that of AtTPC1, although all three luminal Ca2+ sensor sites 1–3 were functional (Figure 8) and resulted in AtTPC1-like luminal Ca2+ sensitivity and voltage dependence of PpTPC1a (Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and supported by Figure 8 showing sequence alignment.

claim: In the absence of luminal Ca2+, the current voltage curves (Iss/Cm(V)) and activation voltage curves (G/Gmax(V)) of the double and triple AtTPC1 mutants appeared shifted to more negative voltages by about 30 mV compared to wild-type AtTPC1.
source: In addition, in the absence of luminal Ca2+, the current voltage curves (Iss/Cm(V)) and even more so the activation voltage curves (G/Gmax(V)) of the double and triple AtTPC1 mutants appeared shifted to more negative voltages by about 30 mV compared to wild-type AtTPC1 (Figures 2B and 5A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 2B, 5A, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1 showing voltage-dependent data.

claim: The changed voltage dependence of both AtTPC1 mutants was reflected in V1 and V2 values similar to VfTPC1.
source: The changed voltage dependence of both AtTPC1 mutants was reflected in V1 and V2 values similar to VfTPC1 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5B showing midpoint voltage data.

claim: When the two AtTPC1 mutants faced 10 mM luminal Ca2+, the current and activation voltage curves as well as the V1, V2 values resembled those of VfTPC1.
source: When the two AtTPC1 mutants faced 10 mM luminal Ca2+, again the current and activation voltage curves as well as the V1, V2 values resembled those of VfTPC1 (Figures 2B and 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 2B and 5 showing voltage-dependent data.

claim: AtTPC1 channels carrying the VfTPC1 polymorphisms (i.e., double or triple residue substitutions) exhibit a low luminal Ca2+ susceptibility.
source: The fact that AtTPC1 channels carrying the VfTPC1 polymorphisms (i.e., double or triple residue substitutions) exhibit a low luminal Ca2+ susceptibility is best displayed by the channel behavior to 50 mM Ca2+.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the Ca2+ sensitivity data.

claim: The current and voltage activation curves (Iss/Cm(V), G/Gmax(V)) of the AtTPC1 mutants and VfTPC1 showed similar strong SV channel activity even at 50 mM luminal Ca2+.
source: The current and voltage activation curves (Iss/Cm(V), G/Gmax(V)) of the AtTPC1 mutants and VfTPC1, however, showed similar strong SV channel activity even at this extreme luminal Ca2+ level (Figures 2B and 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 2B and 5 showing voltage-dependent data.

claim: The E605A/D606N exchange is already sufficient to provide AtTPC1 with the voltage and Ca2+ sensitivity of VfTPC1.
source: Thus, the E605A/D606N exchange is already sufficient to provide AtTPC1 with the voltage and Ca2+ sensitivity of VfTPC1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the mutagenesis data.

claim: The additional E457N replacement in the AtTPC1 E605A/D606N mutant background did not further affect the transition from an Arabidopsis-like to a VfTPC1-like gating behavior.
source: The additional E457N replacement in the AtTPC1 E605A/D606N mutant background, however, did not further affect the transition from an Arabidopsis-like to a VfTPC1-like gating behavior, nor did it further reduce luminal Ca2+ sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the mutagenesis data.

claim: The additional E457N replacement in the AtTPC1 E605A/D606N mutant background did not further reduce luminal Ca2+ sensitivity.
source: The additional E457N replacement in the AtTPC1 E605A/D606N mutant background, however, did not further affect the transition from an Arabidopsis-like to a VfTPC1-like gating behavior, nor did it further reduce luminal Ca2+ sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the mutagenesis data.

claim: Neutral residues at site 457 (E → N/Q) in AtTPC1 made the channel significantly less sensitive to luminal Ca2+ but attenuated voltage-dependent activation compared to wild-type channels.
source: Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2011 reported that neutral residues at site 457 (E → N/Q) in AtTPC1 made the channel significantly less sensitive to luminal Ca2+ but attenuated voltage-dependent activation compared to wild-type channels, as midpoint voltages (V1, V2) were shifted to more positive values.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: The hyperactivity of the native V. faba TPC1 channel is most likely related to the altered Ca2+ sensor site 3 rather than to Ca2+ sensor site 2.
source: Thus, the hyperactivity of the native V. faba TPC1 channel is most likely related to the altered Ca2+ sensor site 3 rather than to Ca2+ sensor site 2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the mutagenesis data.

claim: The two Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 with their residues E457 and E605/D606, respectively, do not have additive effects on channel gating.
source: Considering further the similar luminal Ca2+ sensitivity of E605A/D606N and E457N/E605A/D606N (Figure 5C), the two Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 with their residues E457 and E605/D606, respectively, do not have additive effects on channel gating.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the Ca2+ sensitivity data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The biochemical behavior of VfTPC1 was significantly different than that of AtTPC1.
source: Surprisingly, the biochemical behavior of VfTPC1 was significantly different than that of AtTPC1 and we were unable to recover any usable material after purification.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on protein purification attempts.

claim: A homology model of VfTPC1 was constructed using the high-resolution cryoEM structure of Ca2+-bound AtTPC1-D454N (fou2) as a template.
source: Hence, we constructed a homology model of VfTPC1 using our high-resolution cryoEM structure of Ca2+-bound AtTPC1-D454N (fou2) as a template (Figure 9, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and the model is shown in Figure 9.

claim: The luminal pore entrance operates an inhibitory Ca2+ sensor (site 3) that is coupled to the functional VSD2.
source: From our previous structures of wild-type AtTPC1 and fou2 (Dickinson et al., 2022; Kintzer and Stroud, 2016), we determined that the luminal pore entrance operates an inhibitory Ca2+ sensor (site 3) that is coupled to the functional VSD2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on previous structural studies.

claim: In the wild-type and fou2 structures, the three luminal acidic residues (E605, D606, and D607) of site 3 line the conduction pathway upstream of the selectivity filter.
source: In the wild-type and fou2 structures, the three luminal acidic residues (E605, D606, and D607) of site 3 line the conduction pathway upstream of the selectivity filter (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9—figure supplement 1 showing structural details.

claim: In the wild-type crystal structure, E605 binds a divalent metal on the symmetry axis.
source: In the wild-type crystal structure, E605 binds a divalent metal on the symmetry axis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: In the high-resolution structure of fou2, the residues E605, D606, and D607 rearrange to interact with the hydration shell around a bound metal in the selectivity filter.
source: In our high-resolution structure of fou2 (Dickinson et al., 2022), we showed that these residues rearrange to interact with the hydration shell around a bound metal in the selectivity filter and that D606 in fou2 moves to the position of E605 in the wild-type structure, suggesting that both acidic residues regulate channel function.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to the structural study.

claim: D606 in fou2 moves to the position of E605 in the wild-type structure.
source: In our high-resolution structure of fou2 (Dickinson et al., 2022), we showed that these residues rearrange to interact with the hydration shell around a bound metal in the selectivity filter and that D606 in fou2 moves to the position of E605 in the wild-type structure, suggesting that both acidic residues regulate channel function.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to the structural study.

claim: Both E605 and D606 regulate channel function.
source: In our high-resolution structure of fou2 (Dickinson et al., 2022), we showed that these residues rearrange to interact with the hydration shell around a bound metal in the selectivity filter and that D606 in fou2 moves to the position of E605 in the wild-type structure, suggesting that both acidic residues regulate channel function.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from structural data.

claim: Neutralization of the acidic residues A607 and N608 in the luminal pore entrance of VfTPC1 (equivalent to E605 and D606 in AtTPC1) clearly alters the electrostatics of the pore.
source: In our homology model of VfTPC1, neutralization of the acidic residues A607 and N608 in the luminal pore entrance (equivalent to E605 and D606 in AtTPC1) clearly alters the electrostatics of the pore.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the homology model.

claim: The neutralizing substitutions in VfTPC1 almost certainly prevent the pore entrance from binding the inhibitory Ca2+ observed in the wild-type structure.
source: These substitutions almost certainly prevent the pore entrance from binding the inhibitory Ca2+ observed in the wild-type structure (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1), and from interacting with the water network in the pore as seen in fou2 (Dickinson et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the structural model shown in Figure 9.

claim: The neutralizing substitutions in VfTPC1 prevent the pore entrance from interacting with the water network in the pore as seen in fou2.
source: These substitutions almost certainly prevent the pore entrance from binding the inhibitory Ca2+ observed in the wild-type structure (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1), and from interacting with the water network in the pore as seen in fou2 (Dickinson et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the structural model.

claim: Recent MD simulations with AtTPC1 indicated that the E605/D606 motif is structurally very flexible and adapts according to the direction of ion flow.
source: Recent MD simulations with AtTPC1 (Navarro-Retamal et al., 2021) additionally indicated that the E605/D606 motif is structurally very flexible and adapts according to the direction of ion flow.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to MD simulations.

claim: The efflux from the cytosol to the lumen stabilizes the position found in the hyperactive fou2 mutant, that is, the open channel.
source: This may suggest a valve-like regulatory mechanism: The efflux from the cytosol to the lumen stabilizes the position found in the hyperactive fou2 mutant, that is, the open channel.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a speculative mechanism based on MD simulations.

claim: Influx from the lumen to the cytosol drives the E605/D606 loop toward the pore, fostering channel closing.
source: In contrast, influx from the lumen to the cytosol drives the E605/D606 loop toward the pore, fostering channel closing.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a speculative mechanism based on MD simulations.

claim: Higher luminal Ca2+ increases the probability of Ca2+ to occupy the coordination site at the luminal entrance of the selectivity filter which stabilized the E605/D606 motif in the pore-facing conformation.
source: The MD simulations further suggest a Ca2+-dependent interaction between the E605/D606 motif and a Ca2+ coordination site at the luminal entrance of the selectivity filter (D269/E637; in VfTPC1: D271/E639). Higher luminal Ca2+ increases the probability of Ca2+ to occupy the coordination site which stabilized the E605/D606 motif in the pore-facing conformation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on MD simulations.

claim: Neutralizing E605A/D606N mutations would reduce electrostatic interactions and result in channels that open with less activation energy.
source: Neutralizing E605A/D606N mutations would reduce electrostatic interactions and result in channels that open with less activation energy.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the structural and MD simulation data.

claim: An altered Ca2+-binding site at the luminal pore entrance of VfTPC1 – compared with AtTPC1 – shifts the voltage activation threshold to more negative values.
source: This effect could explain how an altered Ca2+-binding site at the luminal pore entrance of VfTPC1 – compared with AtTPC1 – shifts the voltage activation threshold to more negative values.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the structural and functional data.

claim: The difference in the voltage activation profile between AtTPC1 and VfTPC1 may have been further enhanced by a luminal Mg2+ effect on the intact luminal pore E605/D606 motif of AtTPC1 wild type.
source: The difference in the voltage activation profile between AtTPC1 and VfTPC1 may have been further enhanced by a luminal Mg2+ effect on the intact luminal pore E605/D606 motif of AtTPC1 wild type.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a speculation about additional factors.

claim: Luminal Mg2+ inhibits the AtTPC1 channel but with a much lower efficiency than Ca2+.
source: Like Ca2+, also luminal Mg2+ inhibits the AtTPC1 channel but with a much lower efficiency than Ca2+ (Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2011; Pottosin et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to previous studies.

claim: Under symmetric K+ conditions (100 mM) a single-channel conductance of about 80 pS was determined for AtTPC1 wild type.
source: Under symmetric K+ conditions (100 mM) a single-channel conductance of about 80 pS was determined for AtTPC1 wild type (Figure 11B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 11 showing single-channel recordings.

claim: The neutralizations in the AtTPC1 double mutant E605A/D606A resulted in the removal of a total of four negative charges at the luminal pore entrance.
source: With respect to the dimeric structure of TPC1, the neutralizations in the AtTPC1 double mutant E605A/D606A resulted in the removal of a total of four negative charges at the luminal pore entrance.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a structural consideration.

claim: The unitary conductance of the AtTPC1 double mutant E605A/D606A remained unchanged compared to wild type.
source: Nevertheless, the unitary conductance of the mutant remained unchanged.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on single-channel recordings.

claim: VfTPC1 had a threefold higher unitary conductance than AtTPC1 (250 pS).
source: Moreover, VfTPC1 had a threefold higher unitary conductance than AtTPC1 (250 pS, Figure 11; SchulzLessdorf and Hedrich, 1995), despite its neutral luminal pore residues at the homologous sites to AtTPC1 (E605, D606).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 11 showing single-channel recordings.

claim: The luminal polymorphic pore residues of Ca2+ sensor site 3 apparently do not contribute to the conductance of TPC1.
source: These facts indicate that, in contrast to the AtTPC1-D269/E637 (VfTPC1-D271/E639) Ca2+ coordination site at the luminal entrance of the selectivity filter (Navarro-Retamal et al., 2021), these luminal polymorphic pore residues of Ca2+ sensor site 3 apparently do not contribute to the conductance of TPC1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the conductance data.

claim: The increased activity of the AtTPC1 channel mutant fou2 leads to a hyperexcitability of the vacuole.
source: The increased activity of the AtTPC1 channel mutant fou2 leads to a hyperexcitability of the vacuole (Jaślan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: After the depolarizing current stimulus, the vacuole membrane equipped with VfTPC1 channels remained depolarized at a voltage of about 0 mV during the entire subsequent recording period of 10 s, regardless of the stimulus intensity.
source: After the depolarizing current stimulus, the vacuole membrane equipped with VfTPC1 channels remained depolarized at a voltage of about 0 mV (i.e., at the equilibrium potential for K+) during the entire subsequent recording period of 10 s, regardless of the stimulus intensity (Figure 12, Figure 12—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12 showing voltage recordings.

claim: When AtTPC1-equipped vacuoles were challenged with even the highest current stimulus (1 nA), the post-stimulus voltage remained depolarized for only a short period (tplateau ~ 0.4 s) before relaxation to the resting voltage occurred.
source: In contrast, when AtTPC1-equipped vacuoles were challenged with even the highest current stimulus (1 nA), the post-stimulus voltage remained depolarized for only a short period (tplateau ~ 0.4 s, Figure 12—source data 1) before relaxation to the resting voltage occurred.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12 showing voltage recordings.

claim: The presence of the AtTPC1 triple mutant in the vacuole membrane strongly prolonged the lifetime of the depolarized post-stimulus voltage-plateau phase at all current stimuli compared to AtTPC1 wild type.
source: In comparison to AtTPC1 wild type, the presence of the AtTPC1 triple mutant in the vacuole membrane strongly prolonged the lifetime of the depolarized post-stimulus voltage-plateau phase at all current stimuli (Figure 12).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12 showing voltage recordings.

claim: All other five AtTPC1-triple mutant vacuoles already responded to the lowest current pulses such as 10, 30, or 70 pA with sustained post-stimulus depolarization over the entire recording period.
source: Except of one vacuole, all other five AtTPC1-triple mutant vacuoles already responded to the lowest current pulses such as 10, 30, or 70 pA with sustained post-stimulus depolarization over the entire recording period (Figure 12—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12—source data 1.

claim: AtTPC1-triple mutant vacuoles were hyperexcitable, behaving very much like the VfTPC1 vacuoles.
source: Thus, AtTPC1-triple mutant vacuoles were also hyperexcitable, behaving very much like the VfTPC1 vacuoles.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the excitability data.

claim: At physiological luminal Ca2+ concentration (0.2 mM), the voltage activation threshold of both VfTPC1 and the AtTPC1 triple mutant E457N/E605A/D606N was close to the resting membrane voltage.
source: The further analysis of the corresponding TPC1 currents of these vacuoles revealed, that at this physiological luminal Ca2+ concentration (0.2 mM), the voltage activation threshold of both, VfTPC1 and the AtTPC1 triple mutant E457N/E605A/D606N, was close to the resting membrane voltage.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis of TPC1 currents.

claim: AtTPC1 wild type showed a significant shift of the voltage activation threshold toward positive voltages at physiological luminal Ca2+ concentration (0.2 mM).
source: In comparison, AtTPC1 wild type showed a significant shift of the voltage activation threshold toward positive voltages (Figure 12—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12—figure supplement 1 showing voltage activation data.

claim: There is a positive correlation between the vacuolar hyperexcitability and the shifted voltage activation threshold of the hyperactive TPC1 channels.
source: This points to a positive correlation between the vacuolar hyperexcitability and the shifted voltage activation threshold of the hyperactive TPC1 channels (Figure 12, Figure 12—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the excitability and voltage activation data.

claim: A computational model was used to simulate activation of voltage-dependent TPC1-mediated vacuole excitability.
source: In the following we used a computational model to simulate activation of voltage-dependent TPC1-mediated vacuole excitability (Figure 13; Jaślan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and the model results are shown in Figure 13.

claim: The duration of the post-stimulus voltage-plateau phase (tplateau) was found to depend on the stimulus strength in the computational model.
source: In the simulation too, the duration of the post-stimulus voltage-plateau phase (tplateau) was found to depend on the stimulus strength (Figure 13C, E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 13 showing simulation results.

claim: The voltage activation threshold of TPC1 had an additional influence on tplateau in the computational model.
source: The voltage activation threshold of TPC1 had an additional influence on tplateau.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on simulation results.

claim: A negatively shifted TPC1 activation curve provoked that the vacuole membrane remained in the excited state after stimulation in the computational model.
source: A negatively shifted TPC1 activation curve (Figure 13A, black) provoked that the vacuole membrane remained in the excited state after stimulation (Figure 13B, black).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 13 showing simulation results.

claim: A positively shifted TPC1 activation curve shortened the plateau phase and thus the time course of the excited state in the computational model.
source: A positively shifted TPC1 activation curve (Figure 13A, pink), however, shortened the plateau phase and thus the time course of the excited state (Figure 13B, D, pink).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 13 showing simulation results.

claim: Effectors regulating the voltage activation threshold of TPC1 (e.g., Ca2+) tune the sensitivity of the vacuole membrane and shape the duration of the excited state.
source: Thus, effectors regulating the voltage activation threshold of TPC1 (e.g., Ca2+) tune the sensitivity of the vacuole membrane and shape the duration of the excited state.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the simulation results.

claim: Vacuoles equipped with VfTPC1 or the AtTPC1 triple mutant, which both activate more negatively, are hyperexcitable compared to AtTPC1-expressing vacuoles.
source: In comparison to AtTPC1-expressing vacuoles, those equipped with VfTPC1 or the AtTPC1 triple mutant, which both activate more negatively, are hyperexcitable (Figure 12).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12 showing excitability data.

claim: VfTPC1 is a TPC1 channel variant with gating behavior that is clearly distinct from the A. thaliana AtTPC1 channel of Brassicaceae.
source: We identified the fabaceae prototype VfTPC1 channel from V. faba as a TPC1 channel variant with gating behavior that is clearly distinct from the A. thaliana AtTPC1 channel of Brassicaceae.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the main finding.

claim: The dual polymorphism of two residues within the Ca2+ sensor site 3 in the luminal pore entrance is most likely responsible for the different gating behavior between VfTPC1 and AtTPC1.
source: The dual polymorphism of two residues within the Ca2+ sensor site 3 in the luminal pore entrance is most likely responsible for this different gating behavior, because double loss-of-function mutations in Ca2+ sensor site 3 of AtTPC1 resulted in VfTPC1-like AtTPC1 channels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the mutagenesis data.

claim: Reverse mutations did not convert the features of VfTPC1 to AtTPC1, suggesting that additional structural adaptations have evolved.
source: Reverse mutations, however, did not convert the features of VfTPC1 to AtTPC1, suggesting that additional structural adaptations have evolved and counteract these efforts to gain function in terms of greater voltage and luminal Ca2+ dependence.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the reverse mutagenesis results.

claim: E605 and D606 play the most important role within the triad of site 3 in gating control in AtTPC1.
source: Earlier (Dickinson et al., 2022), we proposed that Ca2+ sensor site 3 in AtTPC1 is formed by three negatively charged residues (E605, D606, and D607). Here, we have now found that E605 and D606 play the most important role within this triad of site 3 in gating control in AtTPC1 (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the mutagenesis data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Neutral residues at Ca2+ sensor site 3, as naturally already present in VfTPC1 (A607/N608), uncouple luminal Ca2+ coordination from gating.
source: Neutral residues at this site, as naturally already present in VfTPC1 (A607/N608; Figure 6), uncouple luminal Ca2+ coordination from gating (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the functional and sequence data.

claim: VfTPC1 features may be even more widespread in the plant kingdom than AtTPC1 features.
source: In fact, these VfTPC1 features may be even more widespread in the plant kingdom, because TPC1 channels from some other plant species like for example Lotus japonicus, Oryza sativa, and Hordeum vulgare also exhibit the neutralizing triple-polymorphism characteristic of VfTPC1 in the luminal Ca2+ sensor sites 2 and 3 (Figures 6 and 8).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on sequence analysis shown in Figures 6 and 8.

claim: The fabacean TPC1 channel from L. japonicus shows a VfTPC1-like gating behavior and low luminal Ca2+ sensitivity as TPC1 currents can still be recorded at 50 mM luminal Ca2+.
source: In well agreement with this triple polymorphism, the fabacean TPC1 channel from L. japonicus shows a VfTPC1-like gating behavior and low luminal Ca2+ sensitivity as TPC1 currents can still be recorded at 50 mM luminal Ca2+ (see Appendix 1—figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by Appendix 1—figure 1 showing electrophysiological data.

claim: Voltage- and Ca2+-dependent TPC1 current responses from mesophyll vacuoles of the monocots O. sativa and H. vulgare appear to exhibit a lower luminal Ca2+ sensitivity and higher probability to open at more negative voltages, respectively.
source: Similarly, voltage- and Ca2+-dependent TPC1 current responses from mesophyll vacuoles of the monocots O. sativa and H. vulgare appear also to exhibit a lower luminal Ca2+ sensitivity and higher probability to open at more negative voltages, respectively (Dadacz-Narloch et al., 2013; Lenglet et al., 2017; Pottosin et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to previous studies.

claim: Luminal pore polymorphism could allow species to adapt the electrical properties of the vacuole to given individual environmental settings.
source: Such luminal pore polymorphism, feeding back on gating behavior of TPC1 channels, could allow species to adapt the electrical properties of the vacuole to given individual environmental settings.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation about the functional significance of TPC1 polymorphism.

claim: Population-based evolutionary genomic approaches have pinpointed a polymorphic pore residue in the vicinity of the TPC1 selectivity filter of Arabidopsis arenosa populations adapted to non-serpentine and serpentine soils.
source: In support of this hypothesis population-based evolutionary genomic approaches have pinpointed a polymorphic pore residue – other than the E605/D606 motif – in the vicinity of the TPC1 selectivity filter of Arabidopsis arenosa populations adapted to non-serpentine and serpentine soils (Arnold et al., 2016; Konečná et al., 2021; Turner et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to evolutionary genomic studies.

claim: TPC1 channels are involved in control of ion homeostasis in addition to a possible contribution to the vacuolar Ca2+ homeostat.
source: While the functional consequences of this polymorphism for ion permeation remain elusive and subject to future studies, these results suggest that TPC1 channels are also involved in control of ion homeostasis in addition to a possible contribution to the vacuolar Ca2+ homeostat (Dindas et al., 2021; see below).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from evolutionary genomic data.

claim: Rhizobia-triggered nodule formation depends on Ca2+ signals and is accompanied by a pronounced K+ loss from the vacuole during the life span of infected cells in legumes.
source: In legumes, rhizobia-triggered nodule formation depends on Ca2+ signals and is accompanied by a pronounced K+ loss from the vacuole during the life span of infected cells (Fedorova et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to a study on nodule formation.

claim: The peculiar luminal Ca2+ tolerance of legume TPC1 type may promote nodule formation and control ion homeostasis during nodule development.
source: It is tempting to speculate that the peculiar luminal Ca2+ tolerance of legume TPC1 type promote nodule formation and control ion homeostasis during nodule development.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation about the functional significance of legume TPC1 properties.

claim: Cation replacement experiments with TPC1-expressing HEK cells demonstrate the principal ability of VfTPC1 and AtTPC1 to conduct not only K+ and Na+ but also Ca2+ ions.
source: In well agreement with experiments with V. faba vacuoles (Ivashikina and Hedrich, 2005; Ward and Schroeder, 1994), our cation replacement experiments with TPC1-expressing HEK cells demonstrate the principal ability of VfTPC1 and AtTPC1 to conduct not only K+ and Na+ but also Ca2+ ions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on the HEK cell experiments.

claim: Relative permeabilities of TPC1s do not correlate with the actual Ca2+ conductivity.
source: Although relative permeability ratios of PCa/PNa ≈ 5:1 (Table 1) may suggest a high calcium permeability, the reduced single-channel conductance measured with Ca2+ (Ward and Schroeder, 1994) support the recent mechanistic explanation that relative permeabilities of TPC1s do not correlate with the actual Ca2+ conductivity (Navarro-Retamal et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to experimental and simulation studies.

claim: Under physiological, plant cell-like Ca2+ and K+ concentrations and gradients, the fava bean SV/TPC1 channel was predominately conducting K+.
source: Under physiological, plant cell-like Ca2+ and K+ concentrations and gradients, the fava bean SV/TPC1 channel was predominately conducting K+ (SchulzLessdorf and Hedrich, 1995, for review see Hedrich and Marten, 2011; Hedrich et al., 2018; Pottosin and Dobrovinskaya, 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to previous studies.

claim: The K+-starvation transcriptome and the elevated vacuolar Ca2+ content of Arabidopsis leaves equipped with hyperactive fou2 TPC1 channels is consistent with the permeation profile showing predominant K+ conductance.
source: This permeation profile is consistent with the K+-starvation transcriptome and the elevated vacuolar Ca2+ content of Arabidopsis leaves equipped with hyperactive fou2 TPC1 channels (Beyhl et al., 2009; Bonaventure et al., 2007b).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to studies on fou2 mutants.

claim: The luminal Ca2+-binding sites of TPC1 or the susceptibility of TPC1 to block by elevated luminal Ca2+ may be the key for the Ca2+ storage capacity of the plant vacuole.
source: The latter suggests that the luminal Ca2+-binding sites of TPC1 or, in other words, the susceptibility of TPC1 to block by elevated luminal Ca2+ may be the key for the Ca2+ storage capacity of the plant vacuole.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the fou2 phenotype.

claim: A much lower luminal Ca2+ sensitivity would keep TPC1 functional even at high luminal vacuolar Ca2+ levels.
source: At the same time, a much lower luminal Ca2+ sensitivity would then keep TPC1 functional even at high luminal vacuolar Ca2+ levels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference about the functional consequences of low Ca2+ sensitivity.

claim: Studies on TPC1 overexpressing and loss-of-function Arabidopsis mutants showed that the AtTPC1 activity modulates the speed and not the amplitude of traveling Ca2+ waves in roots triggered by salt stress.
source: Intruigingly, studies on TPC1 overexpressing and loss-of-function Arabidopsis mutants showed that the AtTPC1 activity modulates the speed and not the amplitude of traveling Ca2+ waves in roots triggered by salt stress (Choi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to a study on Ca2+ waves.

claim: Quantitative analysis of local and distant Ca2+ waves in leaves elicited by wounding excluded the role of TPC1 channels as a CICR element in the vacuole membrane.
source: Quantitative analysis of local and distant Ca2+ waves in leaves elicited by wounding, however, excluded the role of TPC1 channels as a CICR element in the vacuole membrane (Bellandi et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to a study on Ca2+ waves.

claim: TPC1-triggered vacuole excitation could cause the release of Ca2+ from the vacuole to the cytosol via a Ca2+ homeostat with a striking correlation between the duration of excitation and the amount of released Ca2+.
source: Alternatively, TPC1-triggered vacuole excitation could cause the release of Ca2+ from the vacuole to the cytosol via a Ca2+ homeostat (i.e., a combination of yet-to-be identified Ca2+ transporters, Dreyer, 2021) with a striking correlation between the duration of excitation and the amount of released Ca2+ (Dindas et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to studies on Ca2+ homeostasis.

claim: The control of the voltage activation threshold of TPC1 by luminal Ca2+ would directly influence the excitation duration of the vacuole membrane and Ca2+ release in turn.
source: In such a model scenario, the control of the voltage activation threshold of TPC1 by luminal Ca2+ (Figure 5) would directly influence the excitation duration of the vacuole membrane (Figures 12 and 13E) and Ca2+ release in turn.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculative model based on the experimental data.

claim: Tuning of the TPC1 activity by luminal Ca2+ would have the potential to mitigate or even counterbalance the electro-chemical potential of a larger Ca2+ gradient.
source: Without such a regulatory process, a higher luminal Ca2+ concentration would imply a larger transmembrane Ca2+ gradient and therefore the release of a larger Ca2+ quantum. Tuning of the TPC1 activity by luminal Ca2+ would thus have the potential to mitigate or even counterbalance the electro-chemical potential of a larger Ca2+ gradient.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculative mechanism.

claim: A higher luminal Ca2+ concentration downregulates TPC1 activity, which in turn would reduce the excitation duration and would result in a shortened Ca2+ release of larger amplitude.
source: A higher luminal Ca2+ concentration downregulates TPC1 activity, which in turn would reduce the excitation duration and would result in a shortened Ca2+ release of larger amplitude.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculative mechanism.
